[=IL Cheat Sheet=]

[*Scope:*] Quick reminder for the `.ILT` text parsed by [.txt|mIL_Parser.] and emitted by [.txt|ToILT().].
For the pipeline and runtime meaning, see [<../doc_ai/20_pipeline/21_compilation_pipeline.wiki|21_compilation_pipeline.wiki>] and [<../doc_ai/30_runtime/31_vm_and_modules.wiki|31_vm_and_modules.wiki>].

[=How IL Sits In The Repo=]

- surface [.txt|.SPO.] lowers to [.txt|mIL_AST.tModule.]
- `.ILT` is the shared backend text boundary
- canonical examples live in [.txt|SPO_CS/Modules/*.ILT.] and [.txt|SPO_CS/Regression.Tests/*.ILT.]

[=Module Shape=]

[.txt
|§TYPES
|    t_0 := [EMPTY_TYPE => BOOL]
|    t_1 := [EMPTY_TYPE => t_0]
|
|§DEF d_0 € t_1
|    r_0 := FALSE
|    §RETURN r_0 IF TRUE
.]

- all type definitions come first
- each [.txt|§DEF.] has an id, a type id, and a command body
- the last definition is the module init / entry proc

[=Common Names=]

- [.txt|t_*.]
  compiler-assigned type ids
- [.txt|d_*.]
  compiler-assigned def ids
- [.txt|r_*.]
  register ids
- [.txt|_Name.]
  lowered user-visible names and import fields

Common fixed values that appear directly in IL:

- [.txt|EMPTY.]
- [.txt|TRUE.], [.txt|FALSE.]
- [.txt|ONE.]
- [.txt|ARG.], [.txt|ENV.], [.txt|OBJ.], [.txt|RES.]
- runtime type values such as [.txt|INT_TYPE.] and [.txt|BOOL_TYPE.] may appear in type-literal lowering

[=Common Type Forms=]

[.txt
|EMPTY_TYPE
|BOOL
|INT
|[A, B]
|[A | B]
|[#Tag A]
|[Arg => Res]
|[Obj : [Arg => Res]]
|[§VAR A]
|[§FREE]
|[§REC t => Body]
|[§ALL t => Body]
|[§ANY t => Body]
|[.tGeneric tValue]
.]

Notes:

- IL uses [.txt|§REC.], [.txt|§ALL.], and [.txt|§ANY.] where SPO surface syntax uses [.txt|§RECURSIVE.], [.txt|§GENERIC.], and [.txt|§INTERFACE.].
- method types in IL are written as object type plus function type, for example [.txt|[tObj : [tArg => tRes]].]
- [.txt|[A & Proof].] is parser-visible as [.txt|TypeCond.], but it is not fully finished end-to-end

[=Common Command Forms=]

[.txt
|r_1 := 1
|r_2 := TRUE
|r_3 := r_1, r_2
|r_4 := §1ST r_3
|r_5 := §2ND r_3
|r_6 := +#Result r_5
|r_7 := {rec} #Field
|r_8 := .Func ARG
|r_9 := §OBJ:Method ARG
|r_10 := §VAR r_1
|r_11 := §VAR r_10 ->
|§VAR r_10 <- r_1
|§RETURN r_11 IF TRUE
|§RETURN r_11 IF_NOT_EMPTY
|r_12 := §TRY ARG AS_EMPTY
.]

The forms you will see most often in checked-in `.ILT` files are:

- register assignment
- tuple/pair decomposition via [.txt|§1ST.] and [.txt|§2ND.]
- prefix construction and removal via [.txt|+#Tag.] and [.txt|-#Tag.]
- function calls via [.txt|.name arg.]
- method-style calls via [.txt|§OBJ:name arg.]
- var create/get/set via [.txt|§VAR.]
- conditional return via [.txt|§RETURN value IF cond.] or [.txt|IF_NOT_EMPTY.]
- match helpers encoded through [.txt|#Result ...] versus [.txt|EMPTY.]

[=Parser-Visible Extras=]

[.txt
|r_1 := §TRY x AS_BOOL
|r_2 := §TRY x AS_INT
|r_3 := §TRY x AS_PAIR
|r_4 := §TRY x AS_RECORD
|r_5 := §TRY x AS_VAR
|r_6 := §TRY x AS_REF
|r_7 := §TRY x AS_TYPE
|r_8 := §TRY_REMOVE #Tag FROM x
.]

- some of these forms are parser-visible before they are uniformly runtime-complete
- use [<../doc_ai/40_verification/42_known_limits_and_extension_points.wiki|42_known_limits_and_extension_points.wiki>] for the current gap map

[=SPO vs IL Notation=]

[| [*Concept*] | [*SPO*] | [*IL*] |]
[| recursive type | [.txt|[§RECURSIVE t T].] | [.txt|[§REC t => T].] |]
[| generic type | [.txt|[§GENERIC t T].] | [.txt|[§ALL t => T].] |]
[| interface type | [.txt|[§INTERFACE t T].] | [.txt|[§ANY t => T].] |]
[| method type | [.txt|[Obj : Arg => Res].] | [.txt|[Obj : [Arg => Res]].] |]
